key_insight: Collective PV self-consumption is more economically durable than individual operation, because coordination and allocation rules matter more than adding storage under current low-price, low-remuneration markets.
engineering_relevance: For distributed energy system design, the paper shows that governance-aware sharing strategies can improve capacity sizing, cost, and local utilization without requiring technically complex upgrades.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural community sharing one PV facility across 24 users.
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing allocation schemes.
Evaluated configurations with and without battery storage under current market and regulatory conditions.
evidence_signal: The study uses real community load data and scenario comparison to assess annual savings, required PV capacity, benefit distribution, and self-consumption under declining electricity prices.
watch_item: Battery storage has limited value in the current tariff environment, and gains from dynamic sharing can be offset by added governance and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
